You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-08-states-responsive-a11y-terms.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file:line, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED. Inventory + diagnosis, no design proposals.

YOUR AUDIT: UI STATES / RESPONSIVE / ACCESSIBILITY / TERMINOLOGY / COPY.
1. LOADING STATES: every loading.tsx; every skeleton component; every spinner implementation (count distinct spinners); pages that show nothing while loading; long-running action feedback (provisioning, reboot, DNS propagation, payment) — what the user sees, with file refs; use of Suspense; optimistic updates.
2. EMPTY STATES: for every list/table/collection in the portal (servers, games, hosting, sites, domains, mailboxes, volumes, invoices, tickets, activity, team, ssh keys, snapshots, backups, dns records, etc.) what the empty state shows (text + CTA + illustration) and how many distinct empty-state implementations exist.
3. ERROR STATES: error.tsx files, error boundaries, how API errors are surfaced (toast? inline? alert?), the actual error copy (grep for 'Something went wrong', 'Failed to', 'Error'), whether errors explain what/why/how-to-fix, retry affordances, 'view technical details' patterns, 404 handling in portal.
4. SUCCESS STATES: after create/deploy/pay/save — what happens (toast? redirect? inline?); any celebration effects (confetti etc.).
5. TOASTS / NOTIFICATIONS: which toast lib(s) (sonner? react-hot-toast? custom?), how many systems, positions, variants; in-app notification center; banners (promo, win-back, warnings, degraded chat, unverified email, overdue).
6. MODALS / DRAWERS / DIALOGS: implementations (headless-ui? radix? custom?), count of distinct implementations, focus trapping, escape/overlay close, confirmation dialog patterns for dangerous actions (do they state what happens / what is lost / reversibility?), typed-confirm patterns.
7. RESPONSIVE: how Shell handles <lg (sidebar drawer? bottom nav?), tables on mobile (overflow-x? stacked cards?), wizards/checkout on mobile, server panel tabs on mobile, charts on mobile, modals on mobile, min-width hazards (grep for min-w-, w-[...px], fixed widths, grid-cols-N without breakpoints), touch targets; list pages that clearly break. If Playwright is installed (check node_modules/playwright or /root scripts) you may render the LIVE site https://nxeon.cloud public pages at 390px ONLY for read-only screenshots — but do NOT log in and do NOT hit the portal; portal analysis stays code-based.
8. ACCESSIBILITY: counts of aria-* attributes, role=, aria-label on icon-only buttons (find icon-only buttons WITHOUT labels), focus-visible styling in globals.css, keyboard support in custom dropdowns/tabs/menus/command palette, prefers-reduced-motion handling, colour-contrast risks (muted text colours on navy — list the text-* utilities used for secondary text and estimate contrast against the navy surfaces from globals.css hex values), form label association (label htmlFor / aria-labelledby counts vs inputs), skip links, heading order, alt text on images (count img without alt), live regions for async status.
9. TERMINOLOGY: build a glossary of every user-facing noun for the same concept and where each appears: server/VPS/instance/machine/node/droplet; game server/game/instance; hosting/website/site/project/app/deployment; domain/zone/DNS; mailbox/email/account; plan/package/tier/size; region/location/datacenter/zone; snapshot/backup/image; deploy/order/create/launch/provision/buy/checkout; team/organization/workspace; wallet/balance/credits; and internal jargon leaking to customers (node IDs, Proxmox, Mailcow, name.com, worker, prisma, sandbox, etc.). Note CTA label inconsistencies (Continue/Next/Deploy/Order/Buy/Pay).
10. COPY TONE: sample 20 headings/subheadings/CTAs across pages to characterise tone inconsistencies (marketing-y vs terse vs technical); any lorem/placeholder/TODO copy; any references to a third-party 'provider' in customer copy (brand rule: Nxeon speaks as the owner); the '47 seconds' tagline is intentional — do not flag it.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~12-line summary with key counts.
